#4273 -- is -remove-unused-globals parsed and honoured?

Produced by `python flagcheck.py`. Every case is the same dxr.exe over
the same repro.hlsl, differing only in the token occupying the
-remove-unused-globals slot. sha256 is over combined stdout+stderr.

  gLooseUnused is an unused LOOSE global (it would land in $Globals).
  Removing it is the documented job of -remove-unused-globals, so its
  disappearance is the behavioural proof the flag was honoured -- exit
  status and the absence of a diagnostic are both insufficient.
  cbuffer cbB is the unused explicit block this issue is about.

           case  exit  gLooseUnused  cbuffer cbB  sha256(first 16)
--------------- ----- ------------- ------------  ----------------
      real-dash     0       removed      present  986ab3c0fd5b4b33
     real-slash     0       removed      present  986ab3c0fd5b4b33
         absent     0          KEPT      present  a43262a4a56ae481
 nonsense-slash     0          KEPT      present  a43262a4a56ae481
  nonsense-dash     1           n/a          n/a  81795e9205ea9925
     misspelled     1           n/a          n/a  d76bf27772c3fbe0

WHAT EACH CASE IS FOR

  real-dash       the reporter's spelling
  real-slash      MSVC-style prefix of the same option
  absent          baseline: the option removed entirely
  nonsense-slash  SKILL.md's silent-ignore control, in the option's own slot
  nonsense-dash   same nonsense with the '-' prefix
  misspelled      the real option minus one character -- proves the exact spelling is what the parser recognises

READINGS

  [PASS] real-dash differs from absent
         the option changes the output, so it is parsed and honoured -- not silently ignored
  [PASS] real-dash and real-slash are byte-identical
         both spellings of the real option reach the same code
  [PASS] nonsense-slash is byte-identical to absent
         /ZZZNONSENSE exits 0 and does nothing: a clean exit proves nothing about a '/'-prefixed flag, exactly as SKILL.md warns
  [PASS] nonsense-dash is diagnosed
         the '-' prefix IS validated by dxr's own option parse, so the silent-ignore hazard is specific to '/'
  [PASS] misspelled is diagnosed
         the parser recognises the exact spelling, so real-dash cannot have been an accidental near-match
  [PASS] cbuffer cbB survives in every case that ran
         the retained block is not a function of the flag at all


VERBATIM

=== real-dash ===
$ <repo>/build/Debug/bin/dxr.exe -E vsMain -remove-unused-globals -remove-unused-functions -extract-entry-uniforms repro.hlsl
[exit] 0
[sha256] 986ab3c0fd5b4b338cb9e43a735ce0053930c95c0538a778a9cd0c0b64035759

cbuffer cbA {
  const float4 gA;
}
;
cbuffer cbB {
  const float4 gB;
}
;
const float4 gLooseUsed;
float4 vsMain(float4 pos : POSITION) : SV_Position {
  return pos * gA + gLooseUsed;
}
